overview.headline: Drag force grows with air density, speed squared, size and shape

keyPoints.point: Drag depends on air density and square of velocity with shape and inclination effects
keyPoints.quote: Drag depends on the density of the air, the square of the velocity

keyPoints.point: Drag equation states that drag is equal to drag coefficient times density with half velocity squared
keyPoints.quote: The drag equation states that drag D is equal to the drag coefficient Cd times the density rho (ρ) times half of the velocity V squared

keyPoints.point: Drag coefficient includes form drag plus skin friction drag plus wave drag and induced drag
keyPoints.quote: The drag coefficient given above includes form drag, skin friction drag, wave drag, and induced drag components.

keyPoints.point: Drag coefficients are almost always determined experimentally using wind tunnel testing
keyPoints.quote: Drag coefficients are almost always determined experimentally using a wind tunnel.

keyTerms.gloss: Single variable that collects complex drag effects into an equation
keyTerms.quote: The drag equation states that drag D is equal to the drag coefficient Cd

keyTerms.gloss: Aerodynamic resistance that depends on density and velocity of air
keyTerms.quote: Drag depends on the density of the air, the square of the velocity

keyTerms.gloss: Measured area such as wing area used to characterize aerodynamic forces
keyTerms.quote: Notice that the area (A) given in the drag equation is given as a reference area.

keyTerms.gloss: Property of air designated by rho in the drag equation
keyTerms.quote: In the equation given above, the density is designated by the letter rho (ρ).

keyTerms.gloss: Combination of density and velocity that sets pressure in Bernoulli equation
keyTerms.quote: The combination of terms “density times the square of the velocity divided by two” is called the dynamic pressure
